newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma's Suu Kyi released from confinement.
newsitem.headline: Burma's Suu Kyi released from confinement.

text.p: Burma's pro-democracy opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi was released on Thursday from confinement at her Rangoon home, an aide said.

"It would be right to say that she has been released from confinement," the aide, who asked not to be named, told Reuters by telephone after Suu Kyi was allowed to leave her lakeside home for a wedding party and national day celebrations.

Suu Kyi, leader of the National League for Democracy (NLD), was permitted by the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) to attend the wedding reception at a restaurant two days after she was confined at her home.

Police continued to bar public access to Suu Kyi's house but she was allowed to join about 200 NLD members and supporters in a ceremony to mark Burma's National Day at the house of a NLD leader, aides said.

The Nobel laureate and daughter of independence hero Aung San, was restricted to her home indefinitely on Tuesday by SLORC following demonstrations by students of the Yangon Institute of Technology (YIT) in Rangoon.

"It's essential and for the good of the country that...there must be understanding among all forces," Suu Kyi, who was released last year from six years' house arrest, told reporters at the wedding reception.
